principal_diagnosis: Subarachnoid Haemorrhage secondary to ruptured Anterior Communicating Artery aneurysm (ICD-10: I60.7)
hospital_course: Patient was admitted to the Neurosurgery ICU for a subarachnoid haemorrhage (SAH) secondary to a ruptured anterior communicating artery (AComm) aneurysm. On day 2 of admission, she underwent endovascular coil embolisation of the AComm aneurysm. Post-procedure, she was started on Nimodipine 60mg Q4H for vasospasm prophylaxis and her blood pressure was managed with IV Labetalol. A repeat CT Head on day 3 showed no new haemorrhage or vasospasm. Her GCS improved to 15/15 by day 4, and physiotherapy was initiated. She was transferred to the ward on day 5 and remained stable until discharge.
procedures: Endovascular coil embolisation of AComm aneurysm
follow_up: Follow up with Neurosurgery OPD in 2 weeks. Repeat CTA brain in 6 weeks to assess coil integrity. Neuropsychology review in 1 month. Monitor BP daily at home. Strict no heavy lifting for 6 weeks. Return immediately if headache recurs or any neurological change. Clinician signature required before discharge.

flags.issue: Patient treated for subarachnoid haemorrhage from a ruptured cerebral aneurysm, a life-threatening condition.
History of anaphylaxis to Sulfa drugs.
Strict adherence to activity restrictions and return precautions is critical for patient safety.
